ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a balanced three-phase circuit. The outer three sides form a delta connection, and each side has an inductor labeled L, so the outer L elements form a balanced delta network. Inside there are three capacitors labeled C; one end of each is connected together at the central common point, and the other ends are respectively connected to the three vertices of the triangle, so the inner C elements form a balanced star network. Reasoning: The problem gives frequency f = 50 Hz, inductor L = 10 mH = 0.01 H. According to the specified method, convert the outer balanced delta inductors into a star. The impedance of each delta branch is Z_delta = jωL, and the equivalent star impedance per phase is Z_Y = Z_delta/3 = jωL/3. Therefore the admittance of each equivalent inductor branch per phase is 1/(jωL/3). The admittance of each phase of the inner capacitor star is jωC. If all line currents are zero, then the total admittance of each phase is zero: 1/(jωL/3) + jωC = 0. Simplifying gives -j·3/(ωL) + jωC = 0, so C = 3/(ω^2 L). Where ω = 2πf = 2π·50 rad/s. Substituting L = 0.01 H: C = 3 / ((2π·50)^2 · 0.01) = 0.00304 F ≈ 3.03 mF.
